The Bajaj Finance desk

A 12-year model built from annual reports and financial statements. It forecasts revenue and profit, values the equity with DCF and FCFE, and benchmarks ROA and ROE against Cholamandalam on a consolidated basis, including Bajaj Housing Finance.

  1. Annual reports and statements

    Source data for the consolidated entity.

  2. FY26 base-year sheet

    AUM, profit, asset quality, balance sheet, market inputs.

  3. 12-year forecast

    Revenue and profit projections.

  4. DCF and FCFE valuation

    Equity value from cash flows to equity.

  5. Peer benchmark

    ROA and ROE against Cholamandalam.

Why FCFE and not FCFF with WACC: for an NBFC, borrowing is the raw material of the business, not a financing choice. So the model values cash flows to equity and discounts them at the cost of equity.

Cost of equity lab

CAPM: risk-free rate + beta × equity risk premium. Move the inputs and compare with FY26 ROE.

Liquid Liabilities

A research paper on human-AI governance of industrial water, still moving toward journal submission.

A framework for governing water with AI

The paper, Liquid Liabilities: A Synergistic Framework for Human-AI Governance in Industrial Water Management, proposes two frameworks for AI-driven water governance in industrial settings and introduces an "Enough Thinking" philosophy. It went through several rounds of peer review before reaching the conference jury.
